title: Ops Embassy: MiniAgent harness for idempotent runbook automation
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a lightweight, embeddable MiniAgent harness ("Ops Embassy") that executes idempotent runbook tasks as first-class units. The harness should let engineers author runbook steps as small, checkpointed agents that can be scheduled, retried, audited, and executed interactively from the Console or programmatically via the operator CLI. This is intended to reduce mean time to repair for common support flows while preserving safety, auditability, and replayability.
scope: Phase 1: runtime and developer ergonomics. Deliver a minimal runtime that can run a subset of runbook primitives (shell, api-call, kv-checkpoint, conditional-branch), expose a small SDK and CLI, emit structured telemetry to Console, and integrate with existing admin RBAC. Phase 2 (follow-up): Console buttons, canary playbooks, and automated escalation flows.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime can execute a defined subset of runbook primitives and persist checkpoints to the persistent store
SDK + CLI to trigger tasks, query status, and fetch logs (versioned API)
All runs produce structured telemetry (trace id, step timing, errors) ingested in Console traces and cost dashboard
Idempotency guarantees: replaying the same run with the same checkpoint does not perform duplicate destructive actions
Integration tests demonstrating recovery from node restart and network partitions
Security: runs respect RBAC and audit log entries are shipped to the audit log cluster
Documentation: quickstart in Confluence and a sample PRD + example runbook in repo
implementation_steps: Design runtime API and minimal DSL subset (owner: Luis) — spec PR in repo
Implement MiniAgent process skeleton with checkpointing layer (owner: Eng-Infra)
Wire telemetry: structured logs -> trace id -> Console ingestion (owner: Observability)
Add CLI bindings and SDK wrappers (owner: DX team)
Create integration test harness that simulates node restart and verifies idempotency (owner: QA)
Security review & RBAC validation against Private deployment matrix (owner: Security)
Documentation and runbook examples; ship initial Confluence quickstart
technical_notes: Checkpoint store: use existing ops-kv cluster (Redis + S3 snapshot) to avoid a new stateful service
Runtime language: prototype in Go (small binary, native concurrency), SDKs will be provided in Go and Python
Queue/backplane: use existing task-queue (BullMQ) with visibility timeout semantics; evaluate moving to durable job queue later
Idempotency strategy: declare each destructive step with a reconciliation key and a compensating noop-if-previous flag; runtime will surface a deterministic outcome
Telemetry: emit OpenTelemetry spans with a stable run_id and step_id; Console will correlate using trace attributes
Safety: built-in dry-run mode and explicit consent flag for steps that modify production (must be enabled by a Console button with 2FA confirmation)
rollout_plan: Stage rollout: (1) internal canary in dev namespace for platform team, (2) opt-in beta for selected SREs with monitoring on latency and error surface, (3) enable for all SREs with feature flag and cost guardrails. Feature flag path: feature.ops_embassy.miniagent -> incremental enable across org units.
testing_plan: Unit tests for runtime primitives and idempotency invariants
Integration test against ops-kv with simulated failures
Chaos test: kill agent process mid-run and verify resume semantics
E2E: sample incident playbook executed via CLI + Console button in staging
